Use the native View Transition API only as progressive enhancement for one selected media element; unsupported routing/browser combinations receive the specified fade, not a custom animation framework. Public sticky behavior is CSS position:sticky; active chapters use IntersectionObserver. Scroll progress may update one CSS variable through a passive, requestAnimationFrame-throttled listener; never set React state every frame. No GSAP dependency is needed.

3D implementation: dynamically import three.js, GLTFLoader and OrbitControls only after activation. Do not add react-three-fiber or a scene framework for these five prototypes. Keep one active canvas; render on demand and during interaction only. Cap DPR at 1.5 and interaction rendering at 30fps on phone, 60fps desktop. Target model transfer at or below 2MB, 150k triangles and two 1024px textures; use an existing compatible optimized asset or fall back to photos. Target deferred 3D JavaScript at or below 250KB gzip. No model reconstruction or asset-production pipeline is part of this days-scale build.

Image/video pipeline: next/image or the existing authorized image pipeline; explicit width/height and sizes; AVIF/WebP for approved marketing derivatives; preserve originals and existing signed-URL permissions. Target first phone poster at or below 140KB, ordinary phone previews at or below 90KB each, public desktop hero poster at or below 260KB. Preload only the actual LCP image. Lazy-load lower images; do not eagerly preload video or models. Existing user uploads need no new transcoding backend.

Performance targets, not claimed measurements: phone initial transfer at or below 600KB before optional video/3D; route JavaScript at or below 180KB gzip where the existing stack permits; LCP at or below 2.5s, CLS below 0.1, INP below 200ms on representative mobile tests. Every route remains intelligible before optional media loads. Pause and dispose media when hidden or leaving its context.

Data and demo provenance: use existing queries and actual field semantics in product surfaces. The isolated Lab may use explicitly labeled Demo data fixtures and permissioned supporting media, but fixtures never populate production queries. Public demonstrations must be visibly identified as demonstrations unless they use consented real records. Never present invented lifetime earnings, paid payouts, reviews, reach or delivered customer work as evidence. Keep all UI text readable HTML; image models never render UI.

Build and review sequence: day 1 tokens, shell and User Home; day 2 Profile and Business Home; day 3 Content and its absence/error states; day 4 public chapters and optional real-model viewer; day 5 screenshot review, responsive repair, accessibility and performance checks. This is a five-prototype presentation sprint with supplied assets and existing bindings, not a promise to rebuild the complete product in five days. Capture 390×844, 320×568, 768px, 1024px, 1280px and 1440×1000px as relevant, plus short recordings of media and scroll behavior. Review the first User Home capture before propagating its components.
visual_system.radius: Canvas regions, rail, dividers and attached payment ledges: 0px. Ordinary media: 6px. Buttons, inputs and business logos: 8px. Desktop menus/dialogs: 12px. Phone sheets: 16px top corners and 0px bottom corners. Personal avatars: circular. Public device frames use their separate physical radii. Do not apply one large radius to every opportunity, person, balance or section. Never clip focus outlines to a decorative shape.

typography.face: Archivo, Google Fonts, load with next/font/google Archivo or licensed self-hosted WOFF2.
typography.weights: Variable 600–800; 700 for money and application headings, 800 for public hero, 700 for wordmark.
typography.role: Display, identity, headings and monetary amounts. Use lining tabular numerals for money.

typography.face: IBM Plex Sans, Google Fonts, load with next/font/google IBM_Plex_Sans or licensed self-hosted WOFF2.
typography.role: Body, task instructions, metadata, navigation, forms, controls and financial explanations.

visual_system.video: User Home may play one directly available Recreate video muted and inline for at most 6 seconds, once per page visit, after the item has been at least 75% visible for 500ms. This is a finite task preview, not an autoplay feed. Show a persistent 44px Pause/Play control, keep money and conditions outside the video, and stop when visibility drops below 50%, the tab hides or another player starts. External-only references remain links; do not generate replacement previews. Reduced motion, Save-Data, reported 2G/slow-2G and autoplay rejection receive the poster and explicit Play. Story video, submitted evidence, Profile work and Content assets start only on explicit activation; no hover-playing grid. Public hero may play a muted 12-second film once: four 3-second shots showing filming, supplied creative in use, real vehicle context and actual content review. It has Pause and Replay and does not gate text. Target 720p mobile at or below 2.5MB and 1080p desktop at or below 4MB. With unavailable footage, slow connection or reduced motion, retain the useful poster and separately understandable chapters. Native playback controls, captions and full-screen inspection remain available; never autoplay audio.
visual_system.theme_strategy: Use authored surface contrast rather than separate light and dark designs for each mode. The primary working canvas is cool-light; the desktop rail, selected media housings and Profile identity masthead are graphite. Financial reading and forms stay light. Public sections can use both, but theme changes follow a change of material or task, not arbitrary alternating stripes. There is no automatic full-app dark-mode toggle in this five-prototype sprint because a partial dark implementation would be worse than a deliberate system. This is a scope decision, not a permanent ban. Support forced colors and browser text settings now.
visual_system.accessibility: Normal text must meet 4.5:1 contrast; large text and necessary non-text controls 3:1. Validate actual combinations, especially dark controls and media edges, rather than assuming an accent is accessible everywhere. No essential text below 14px; body and form inputs remain 16px. Interactive targets are at least 44×44px and primary task actions at least 48px high. All media has an appropriate source label and useful alternative; captions and written instructions convey required actions. No fact depends on motion, hover, color or a 3D view. Preserve semantic navigation, headings, lists, definition lists, forms and actual tab behavior. Provide skip links, Escape dismissal, focus containment only for modal surfaces and focus return to the originating object. Separate Play, Save and detail links; do not nest controls. At 200% text enlargement and 320px effective width, stack compositions and use the adaptive navigation fallback. When the keyboard is open or a fixed task bar exceeds 25% of the visual viewport, move that bar into normal flow. Model interaction must have keyboard controls and an obvious exit. Reduced motion disables autoplay, translation, scroll choreography, automatic rotation and spinner movement while retaining every state and action.
visual_system.money_treatment: Use Archivo 700 with font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums lining-nums and tracking -0.02em. Home opportunity amounts are 30/34px phone and 34/38px desktop; detail amounts 36/40px and 44/48px; available Earnings balance 44/48px and 56/60px. Currency and amount retain equal weight and use the actual locale/currency formatting. Payment basis sits immediately below at IBM Plex Sans 14/20px, never as an unreadable superscript. Recreate pay is white on its opaque cobalt ledge beside, not over, the reference. Story pay is ink beside the intact creative. Car pay is ink in the attached white caption with per month always visible. Do not force all amounts into blue or green: accent indicates a decision, not available or paid money. Opportunity pay is not labeled take-home unless it really is net. Preserve gross/fee/net disclosure and exact server amount semantics. Never truncate, count up, estimate a car total from days, or substitute zero while fetching.
visual_system.backgrounds: Application backgrounds are solid CSS colors: canvas, white surface, graphite housing and underlay letterboxing. There is no noise texture, atmospheric wallpaper, glass blur or random gradient. Public photography is foreground content, not a background behind essential copy. The public Drive fallback and inactive vehicle stage may use a hard horizon built as linear-gradient(180deg,#E6EBF0 0%,#E6EBF0 62%,#D9E1E9 62%,#D9E1E9 100%); this represents a wall/floor division, not a brand glow. The active 3D stage replaces that illustration with the specified physical plane and real lighting. Do not run a full-page WebGL background. Empty states use flat canvas and, when informative, one deterministic 2px-stroke diagram at a maximum 160px size.

type_scale.role: Person identity and work detail title

type_scale.weight: IBM Plex Sans 400; 500 for emphasized facts

type_scale.role: Metadata, payment basis, field label, provenance and status

motion.trigger: Hover, press or keyboard activation of a control.
motion.reduced_motion: Color feedback up to 80ms; focus remains immediate; no displacement.
motion.name: Direct control feedback
motion.what_it_explains: Confirms that a control is actionable. Non-financial buttons may translate down by 1px on press; money controls never move their amount or label.

motion.trigger: A discovery filter or local view changes.
motion.reduced_motion: Indicator and results replace immediately, with at most an 80ms opacity change.
motion.name: Selection edge
motion.what_it_explains: Connects the selected label to its results. Keep previous results clearly identified as updating until the actual response; never animate stale identity data into a new context.

motion.trigger: Opening an opportunity, person, car or selected Content asset where the same source media exists in both states.
motion.reduced_motion: No geometry interpolation; at most a 100ms fade.
motion.name: Selected-media continuity
motion.what_it_explains: The inspected object is the one the person selected. Animate one media rectangle only through progressive enhancement; do not animate money, the whole feed or the navigation shell. Back restores source position and focus.

motion.trigger: Opening or closing a contextual sheet.
motion.reduced_motion: Show immediately or use an 80ms opacity change, retaining focus behavior.
motion.name: Task-edge sheet
motion.what_it_explains: A temporary decision comes from the reachable task edge. Translate at most 48px, without spring or overshoot. Close is always available; dragging is never required.

motion.trigger: A directly playable Recreate is sufficiently visible and media/data preferences allow preview.
motion.name: Bounded work preview
motion.duration_ms: 500 visibility dwell; maximum 6000 playback; 120 poster handoff
motion.easing: Playback at native speed; handoff linear
motion.what_it_explains: Shows what someone would recreate, not how much they could earn. Play once, muted, one player only, with immediate Pause and all task/payment facts visible independently.

motion.trigger: Explicitly selecting another gallery image or Content asset.
motion.reduced_motion: Replace after the next source is ready, without movement.
motion.name: Source handoff
motion.what_it_explains: Changes the selected source while retaining the inspection location. Crossfade imagery only; caption, file state and post state must change with the corresponding record.

motion.trigger: The server confirms save, approval, submission or another actual mutation.
motion.reduced_motion: Immediate literal state replacement and a restrained announcement.
motion.name: Recorded decision
motion.what_it_explains: A real record changed. Use an accent-wash highlight and literal message, not confetti or a reward burst. Different approval and payment consequences retain their correct wording.

motion.trigger: Actual upload-byte updates, or a genuinely pending request.
motion.reduced_motion: Show actual bytes and static loading text.
motion.name: Honest activity
motion.duration_ms: 80 maximum byte interpolation; 900 spinner revolution while an ordinary request is pending
motion.what_it_explains: Transfer follows reported bytes and never interpolates beyond them. Unknown-duration processing and waiting-provider states use static labels, not animated production timelines.

motion.trigger: An actual model finishes loading or the person operates its viewer controls.
motion.reduced_motion: Immediate model appearance and reset; direct user-controlled rotation remains available.
motion.name: Physical inspection
motion.duration_ms: 180 appearance; 220 reset; direct orbit has no tween
motion.what_it_explains: Reveals another view of the same actual vehicle. There is no automatic spin, idle animation, inertia after release or simulated reconstruction.

motion.trigger: Native desktop scrolling through the public earning chapters.
motion.reduced_motion: Three complete static chapter compositions in ordinary flow; no sticky choreography.
motion.name: Public frame progression
motion.duration_ms: Scroll-linked with no timed lag; fallback chapter crossfade 220
motion.what_it_explains: The task changes from making a video to posting supplied creative to physical car advertising. Move the explanatory assembly by at most 24px and a device by at most 8deg; never scrub a fake financial state or hijack scroll.

motion.trigger: An eligible public hero becomes visible and its real film is ready.
motion.name: Public work film
motion.what_it_explains: Connects people doing work with the actual product. Pause responds immediately, playback never blocks the audience actions, and Replay is offered at the end.

what_was_merged: From the evolved Local Edit: source-faithful photographic color, restrained separators and the confidence to leave operational facts unboxed.
From Night Relay: dark full-media inspection and a bounded cinematic public introduction.
Neither alternative's dominant theme was inherited. The chosen system establishes its own graphite/cobalt/light-surface relationship and offset-frame identity.
chosen.name: Frame Shift
chosen.how_it_avoids_ai_slop: Its visual energy comes from specific product objects and their relationships: reference beside payment, intact creative beside posting conditions, real vehicle above a monthly commitment, delivered file beside its decision. There are no generic bento metrics, decorative model blobs, neon glows, floating glass, fake reach charts or synthetic local-business scenes. Generated imagery is governed by provenance rather than a blanket aesthetic prohibition. The interface itself is always built and captured, never image-generated.
chosen.why_it_won: It has the strongest combined forecast across the eleven requested criteria, especially mobile earning clarity, desktop media working quality and purposeful motion. It is not the easiest option: the evolved Local Edit scores better for immediate familiarity and buildability. It is not the most cinematic option either. It wins because its distinctive behavior and geometry continue to work when the footage is paused, a model is absent or a business has no delivered content. These are specification-level judgments to test against real browser captures, not measured results.
chosen.how_it_stays_simple: Keep the existing destinations, one obvious next action and progressive detail. Most screens use normal document flow, native media and familiar controls. Only the selected object gains depth or movement. One player and one model can be active at a time. Money remains still, terms stay readable without playback, and every optional effect has a complete static fallback.

reopened_decisions: Warm paper and vermilion were preferences, not requirements. They competed again and lost as the master palette; their human photographic discipline survives without their color scheme.
A nearly all-light application was unnecessarily restrictive. Graphite now gives identity and media a strong physical presence, while light surfaces serve reading and financial decisions.

Motion does not need to be limited to tiny fades. A selected-media transition, a more substantial sheet and scroll-linked public explanation are justified when they clarify continuity or task differences.

Blanket avoidance of autoplay was too broad as a visual rule. The chosen system permits one finite, muted Recreate preview and a pausable public film, with strict visibility, data and reduced-motion conditions. Evidence review and content grids do not autoplay.

Expressive 3D is welcome when it exposes a real physical object. A view-only real vehicle can appear elegantly in Profile and public explanation. This does not reopen future zone picking, wrap simulation or mandatory scanning.

Generated environments are no longer categorically rejected. They can support explicitly illustrative public or proposal assets. Frame Shift chooses a deterministic studio stage because it explains the object just as well with fewer production dependencies—not because generated environments are forbidden.

Cinematic and product-driven public treatments are now legitimate candidates. The chosen public site uses implemented screens, moving media and scroll-linked staging rather than relying on an editorial photo-and-headline split alone.

Device frames, depth and object overlap can be functional explanation tools. They are used where a visitor needs to understand a real product interaction, not as floating decoration or inside the authenticated app.

The old person rows and persistent desktop context column were visual decisions, not sacred UX. Business Home becomes a work-led comparison gallery, with the same people-first discovery logic and actual attention summaries.
founder_feedback_read: The product reasoning is retained; the visual answer is not. The founder is asking for a recognizable, energetic technology product where paid work and real marketing materials feel tangible—not conservative local-business software dressed in good photography. My earlier prohibitions made one aesthetic seem inevitable. This response reopens palette, theme, typography, depth, media, motion, 3D and public staging, compares three genuinely different approaches and chooses on the whole product rather than on restraint alone. The scores are 1–10 design forecasts, not claims that screenshots, usability, performance or brand recall have already been tested.
